literal: enemy inside timid-person hand bright-sword assembly inside fearing he learned text
translation: The learning of a man who is afraid to speak in an assembly is like a sharp sword in the hands of a coward on the battlefield.
modern: அவையில் பேசப் பயப்படுகிறவன் கற்ற நூலானது, போர்க்களத்தில் பகைவர் நடுவே ஒரு பேடியின் கையில் இருக்கும் கூர்மையான வாளைப் போன்றது.
explanation: This couplet uses a vivid simile to illustrate the uselessness of knowledge if one lacks the courage to share it. It compares a learned person who is terrified of speaking in an assembly to a timid person holding a bright, sharp sword on a battlefield. Just as the sword is of no use to someone too frightened to fight, the texts learned by a scholar are worthless if he is too afraid to present his knowledge before a council. The word 'பேடி' (timid person or coward) emphasizes the complete lack of necessary courage in a critical situation.
